Cr. Appeal (DB) No. 1434 of 2024  Niraj Kumar @ Niraj Mehta ---- --- Appellant  Versus  The State of Jharkhand --- --- Respondent  ---
CORAM: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Rongon Mukhopadhyay Hon'ble Mr. Justice Ambuj Nath ---
For the Appellant: Mr. Jitendra Shankar Singh, Advocate For the Resp.-State: Mr. Vineet Kr.
Vashistha, Special P.P.
---
I.A. No. 4851 of 2025 04 / 07.05.2025 Heard Mr. Jitendra Shankar Singh, learned counsel for the appellant and Mr. Vineet Kr. Vashistha, learned Special P.P.
2.
This application has been preferred by the appellant for grant of bail during the pendency of this appeal.

3. The appellant has been convicted for the offences under sections 366 and 376(3) of the Indian Penal Code and section 6 read with section 5(1) of the POCSO Act and has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for twenty years along with a fine of Rs. 50,000/- for the offence under section 6 of the POCSO Act.
4. It has been alleged that the appellant had enticed away the daughter of the Informant.

5. Submission has been advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant that the evidence of the victim who has been examined as P.W-3 clearly reveals that she was taken to different places and was ultimately kept at Bengaluru, but she has not raised any hue and cry during the entire journey to different places, if at all she was enticed away by the appellant.
It has further been submitted that the appellant is in custody since 26.05.2022.

Learned counsel has drawn the attention of the court to the evidence of the doctor who has been examined as P.W-5 and has submitted that no marks of injury were found on any vital part of the body, which would further indicate that she was not Niraj Kumar @ Niraj Mehta vs The State Of Jharkhand on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137370410/
1 subjected to rape.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel also submits that the Medical Report has assessed the age of the victim as 16 +_ one year and her evidence clearly indicates that there was love affair between the appellant and the victim.
6. Learned A.P.P has opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant.
7. Regard being had to the evidence of the victim who has been examined as P.W-3 as well as the evidence of P.W-5, we are inclined to admit the appellant on bail.

Accordingly, during the pendency of this appeal, appellant, above named, is directed to be released on bail on furnishing bail bonds of Rs. 10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each, to the satisfaction of learned Exclusive Special Judge, POCSO Act, Palamau at Daltonganj in Special POCSO Case No. 55 of 2022.
8. The aforesaid I.A. stands allowed and disposed of.

(Rongon Mukhopadhyay, J) (Ambuj Nath, J) Ranjeet-Nandini/
